Title: Chainsaw

You produce custom chainsaws on demand.
Your chainsaws have at least 5 properties such as length of the "guide bar" (Schwertlaenge), chain width, electric or motor chainsaw.
After your customer told you the properties, you can start ordering the parts from various online sources (in parallel).
After the parts arrive you have to do a manual inspection of all parts, and then assemble the parts.
During production, you regularly send updates to your customer.
After producing the first saw you send it to your customer.
If he likes it, the rest of his order are produced.

args.text: When labeling BPMN activities, use concise verb–object wording that names the action described; preserve distinctions between separate actions rather than substituting a related but different action.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance already covers faithful, distinct activity labels.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.

result.rule: When the description states a specific activity or process-ending outcome: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or end event with a concise phrase that preserves the stated action or outcome; do not substitute a related action or add an unsupported one.

When the description identifies a specific trigger, decision criterion, or performed activity: Use a concise BPMN label that expresses that meaning; do not substitute a related event, outcome, or different decision.

When the description states an activity together with criteria, optional supporting actions, or a later outcome associated with it: Label the BPMN task with a concise verb-object phrase for the activity itself. Keep associated criteria, alternatives, and subsequent outcomes out of the label unless they define the activity.

When the description states an activity with explicit alternatives or qualifiers that distinguish its scope: Label the corresponding BPMN element concisely while preserving those stated distinctions; do not generalize them away.
